title.narrative: Resilient Approaches in Natural ranGeland Ecosystems (RANGE)

description.narrative: Community members (women and youth; livestock owners; ward planning committees), government stakeholders (national, county and ward-level), private sector actors, local governance and peacebuilding structures, land management structures, local and international development partners, research and policy agencies, financial institutions.

Strengthen resilience of the ASAL communities that contributes to sustainable economic and social development in a well-managed landscapeExpected Result 1: Improved rangeland management repairs ecosystem health and increases food, nutrition and water security.Expected Result 2: Sustainable livestock and alternative livelihood production and competitiveness of markets strengthened within an improved policy environment.Expected Result 3: Improved linkages among and between communities and government structures to support collaboration on economic, environmental and social issues promote stability and sustained development.Expected Result 4: Strengthened Research and evidence-based programming contribute to impactful project implementation, effective coordination, early warning and early action, innovation and learning for resilient ASAL communities.

The premise for this ASAL programming is to take to scale the gains of the previous and current ongoing work in the ASALs aimed at strengthening resilience and unlocking the economic potential. It has been established that the ASALs have high economic development potential particularly linked to livestock and blue economy. However to unlock this potential it is noted that some distinct challenges predominant in the ASALs need to be addressed. These include; how to close the developmental gap; how to protect and promote the mobility and institutional arrangements essential to productive pastoralism; how to ensure food and nutrition security across the region, and how best to address the insecurity/conflict element. These challenges have to be addressed against the backdrop of the impact that climate change has on livelihoods and the ASAL landscapes

Intra/Intercommunity dialogues aimed at enhancing peacebuilding and cohesion 4. Launch of the Marsabit County Alternative Justice System 5. Cross-Border Peace Building and Cohesion Dialogues 6. Finalization Workshop for Isiolo County Rangeland Management Regulations 7. Governors' Workshop 8. National Pastoral Summit 9. 4th Pastoralist Leadership Summit 10. Training for the veterinary team in Isiolo County 11. Workshop on Climate Change These events were designed to strengthen community ties, promote peace, and address important issues in the region. A total of 2445 participants participated.
